It solves the problem of T-junctions (cracks) that arise when standard Marching Cubes is applied to hierarchical data by using dual grids and ghost cells to ensure boundary consistency without requiring the entire dataset in a single processor's memory [S1].

The claim states that the method solves T-junctions (cracks) from standard Marching Cubes on hierarchical data by using dual grids and ghost cells to ensure boundary consistency without requiring the entire dataset in a single processor's memory. Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points: 1) T-junctions arise from re-sampling to vertex-centered representation for standard Marching Cubes and are solved by using dual grids (cell centers). 2) Ghost cells are used to extend grids so that data required for stitch cells is available locally, ensuring boundary consistency. 3) This approach allows parallel processing on a per-grid basis, overcoming the limitation of previous methods that required the entire dataset to reside in the memory of a single processor.
